options.text: Because the browser won't paint content until it has built the CSSOM, to avoid a flash of unstyled content
Because CSS files are always larger than JavaScript files
Because CSS runs on the GPU
Because CSS can only load after all images

questions.explanation: The browser needs the full CSSOM before it can render, otherwise it would show unstyled content and then restyle it (a FOUC). So slow/large CSS delays the first paint.

questions.prompt: Put the critical rendering path steps in order.

items.text: Combine them into the render tree

questions.explanation: The browser builds the DOM and CSSOM, merges the visible parts into a render tree, computes layout, paints pixels, and composites the layers into the final frame.

questions.prompt: A plain synchronous <script> is called ____-blocking because it pauses building the DOM until it downloads and runs.
questions.explanation: A synchronous script is parser-blocking: the HTML parser stops constructing the DOM to fetch and execute the script, then resumes.

questions.prompt: Match each script form to when it executes.

pairs.right: Blocks parsing; runs immediately when reached
Runs after parsing finishes, in document order
Runs as soon as it downloads, order not guaranteed

questions.explanation: defer preserves order and waits for parsing; async runs opportunistically without order; modules behave like defer by default; a plain script blocks the parser.

questions.prompt: Which changes help shorten the critical rendering path for the first paint? Select all that apply.

options.text: Defer non-critical scripts instead of blocking in the head
Inline the critical CSS and load the rest without blocking
Reduce the number and size of render-blocking resources

questions.explanation: Fewer and smaller render-blocking resources, deferred non-critical JS, and inlined critical CSS all shorten the path. Adding more blocking stylesheets does the opposite.

questions.prompt: Which pair of properties can typically be animated at the composite step, without forcing layout or paint?
questions.explanation: transform and opacity can usually be handled by the compositor (often on the GPU) without re-running layout or paint, so they animate smoothly.
